However, confidence is not high because the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates that include near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), which domain knowledge flags as likely inflating full-model AUROC and making it non-comparable to PRS-only performance; PRS-only AUC/R2 or covariate-regressed-out metrics are not provided. Competing candidates have cleaner covariate sets but weaker/less comparable metrics (e.g., framework scores like PGS000965/PGS001181) or non-generic endpoints (e.g., checkpoint-inhibitor-induced hypothyroidism). Given the available evidence, PGS005218 is best supported on endpoint focus and method, but the biomarker-adjusted performance reporting prevents a high-quality designation.

Main limitation: the chosen Commun Biol 2024 models have missing PRS-comparable performance metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R2; covariates listed as Unknown), so the ranking relies heavily on method/structure and OR alone, leaving residual uncertainty versus alternatives that report explicit PGS-only metrics.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, though some are subtype/time-to-event endpoints (e.g., M81; TTE without pathological fracture). Several candidates come from pan-trait/portability frameworks (PGS001273/PGS001274: “across 813 traits”; PGS001883/PGS002095: “Portability of 245…”) which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused scores despite having PRS-only AUROC/R2/partial-r reported. Among the remaining non-framework options, PGS002768 is endpoint-faithful (“Osteoporosis”), uses a genome-wide continuous shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with a high variant count (1,091,549) and provides an interpretable per-SD effect size (OR 1.31, moderate) in European evaluation. Competing recent scores (PGS004495/PGS004565/PGS004809/PGS004810 and related M81 variants) lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and mostly report only single effect sizes or incremental R2 with limited context; some also have covariates listed as Unknown, which lowers comparability confidence. Overall, PGS002768 is the best-supported direct-match based on endpoint fidelity + strong method/structure signals, but confidence is limited because across the strongest-looking candidates there is sparse and non-uniform reporting of PRS-only performance metrics, making separation imperfect.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, though some are subtype/time-to-event variants (e.g., M81, TTE). Among the non-framework, endpoint-faithful options, PGS004565 (RFDiseasemetaPRS) provides the strongest visible PRS-discrimination signal via effect size (OR per SD=1.328) and uses an ensemble/meta-PRS method that domain guidance prioritizes over single-score constructions, while maintaining exact osteoporosis phenotyping. Key limitation: for PGS004565 (and its sibling Commun Biol models), covariates are listed as Unknown and there are no PRS-comparable AUROC/R² metrics reported, making it hard to confirm comparability and to distinguish it decisively from close competitors like PGS004560 (OR=1.321) or PGS002768 (OR=1.31) and from framework scores that report PRS-only AUROC/R² (PGS001273/PGS001274) but are penalized as pan-trait UKB framework models and show small incremental AUROC/low PGS-only R².

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, though several are framework-style (e.g., the UKB “813 traits” snpnet models PGS001273/PGS001274 and the “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” models PGS001883/PGS002095), which domain guidance flags as generally underperforming disease-focused scores when alternatives exist. Among the non-framework options, PGS004565 (RFDiseasemetaPRS; OR=1.328222) is endpoint-aligned (phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis) and has the strongest reported per-SD effect size among the osteoporosis-labeled models shown (exceeding PGS002768 OR=1.31 and PGS004495 OR=1.1979), and the method name indicates an ensemble/meta-PRS approach, which domain guidance strongly prefers structurally. Main limitation: the PGS00456x/PGS00449x Commun Biol models have missing PRS-comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²) and ‘covariates: Unknown’, so the evidence does not support a high-confidence, clearly superior choice over the other endpoint-aligned candidates.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to osteoporosis (trait_efo=osteoporosis and phenotyping_reported indicates osteoporosis or ICD10-aligned subtypes). Among them, PGS004810 is best supported structurally: it uses PRSmixPlus (an integrative/mixture approach consistent with the domain preference for aggregation/advanced genome-wide modeling) with a very large variant set (1,876,917) and reports an incremental R²=0.022 (vs 0.011 for its sibling PGS004809), suggesting stronger PRS contribution in its evaluation. Competing options have notable limitations in the visible evidence: the snpnet scores (PGS001273/PGS001274) come from a pan-trait sparse framework and show low PGS-only signal (PGS-only R² ~0.007–0.009; incremental AUROC small), the portability-framework scores (PGS001883/PGS002095) report only modest partial correlations, and several LDpred2/RFDiseasemetaPRS/PRS-CS/PRS-CSx candidates report only effect sizes with unclear comparability (and some have unknown covariates). Remaining limitation: for PGS004810 there is no directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R² reported (only incremental R² in a specific evaluation), and most other candidates also lack clean PRS-only metrics, so the selection is driven mainly by method/structure rather than decisive head-to-head performance evidence.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis), but most lack PRS-comparable performance metrics (AUC/R²) and report only effect sizes or partial correlations, limiting a clearly strong recommendation. PGS001273 is preferred because it has clean endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis; trait_efo: osteoporosis), uses only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and uniquely provides explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.5685; PGS R² no covariates=0.00688) plus incremental AUROC, allowing interpretation without relying on covariate-driven full-model AUROC. Main limitation: PGS001273 originates from a pan-trait sparse UK Biobank framework ("across 813 traits"; snpnet with 316 variants), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly; several newer genome-wide shrinkage/ensemble methods (e.g., PRS-CS/PRS-CSx, PRSmixPlus, RFDiseasemetaPRS) have stronger structural properties but lack comparable PRS-only metrics here, keeping confidence moderate and the overall outcome sub-optimal.

All listed candidates are direct matches for the target concept (testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (mostly “Malignant neoplasm of testis” or “Testicular cancer”). Among the coherent Cancer PRSweb cluster (PGS000595–PGS000604) with identical basic covariates and EUR-only context, PGS000604 is best supported by the strongest reported discrimination/effect evidence within that family (full-model AUROC 0.703 with CI 0.659–0.745; Nagelkerke’s pseudo-R² 0.0882; per-SD OR 2.106 [1.729–2.565]) and larger training/validation sizes than its MGI-trained siblings. Competing direct-match candidates include PGS001164 (snpnet) which uniquely reports PGS-only metrics but is from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a documented generalization-risk archetype) and has modest PGS-only AUROC (~0.63) and low PGS R² (~0.016), and PGS000796 which reports very high full-model metrics but is explicitly a reweighted 52-variant score with no training sample and performance that may be driven by non-PRS components/packaging, reducing comparability. Limitation: most scores (including PGS000604) lack explicit PRS-only discrimination metrics, so selection relies on within-family consistency plus effect-size/full-model signals, lowering confidence from High to Moderate.

All 12 candidates are direct matches to testicular carcinoma via trait_efo/phenotyping (mostly “Malignant neoplasm of testis” or “Testicular cancer”). All listed candidates are direct matches for the target trait (testicular carcinoma) with coherent endpoint fields (e.g., trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: malignant neoplasm of testis or testicular cancer). All 12 candidates are direct matches to testicular carcinoma/testicular cancer by trait fields, with generally endpoint-faithful phenotyping ("Malignant neoplasm of testis" or "Testicular cancer"; PGS000796 is incident-only but still aligned). Limitation: across the disease-focused PRSweb siblings, reported AUROCs are full-model (with basic covariates) rather than clearly PGS-only, so differences may not fully reflect PRS-only performance; this keeps confidence at Moderate rather than High.
